title: Does a query match the sentinel or the sequence delimiter?
body:
The sentinel `$` and the sequence delimiter (`%` by default) are bytes in the text, so a query may match them. On fixture 1 (`ACGTNNACGT$`) the query `$` counts 1 and `ACGTNNACGT$` counts 1. On fixture 2 (`ACGTACGT%ACGTACGT$`) the query `T%A` matches at ABC:7, spanning the boundary between the two sequences. No test pins this today. sufr-5cf0b7 adds one that asserts the current behaviour, so a change here moves that test.

## Options

| option | behaviour | cost |
|---|---|---|
| keep | bytes are bytes; a query may match the sentinel or the delimiter and a match may span sequences | none; the test in sufr-5cf0b7 pins it |
| reject | a query holding the sentinel or the delimiter is an error from `search` | an error path in `search`, and the CLI reports it; a user cannot search for a literal `%` in a text whose delimiter is `%` |
| bound | a match may not cross a sequence boundary; a hit whose match would run into the delimiter or sentinel is not a hit | the compare in `search.rs` has to know where the sequence ends, which the ranks alone do not say; a cost per comparison |

Jack chose to keep on 2026-11-03, as the current behaviour and not as a design decision. The test in sufr-5cf0b7 records it. This issue stays open as the place to decide the other two.
